caption:
Resolution gets the attention. Revisit cadence decides whether you catch anything.

A sharp image of a site from six days ago tells you what happened last week. It does not tell you what is happening now. Between passes, the area of interest goes dark — no matter how fine the pixel. That gap is where activity starts, runs, and finishes before the next look arrives.

A coarser sensor with a tight revisit window will outperform a sharp one with a long gap, every time the thing you care about moves fast — a breach, a flood pulse, a vessel transiting a corridor. Match the cadence to the tempo of the threat. Resolution without revisit is a photograph. Revisit without resolution is still indications and warning.

card.headline: Cadence beats resolution
card.sub: A sharp image from days ago can't see what's happening now. Match revisit rate to how fast the threat moves.

rationale: Explains a real collection trade-off (revisit vs resolution) that hasn't been covered yet, stays product-neutral, and gives the reader a usable mental model.
